skim: India detained more than 2,000 protesters — including three opposition chief ministers, a Supreme Court lawyer and a prominent YouTuber — and cut mobile internet in central Delhi to crush a youth-led “Cockroach Party” rally demanding election chief Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, one of the biggest challenges yet to Modi’s government.

A Houthi missile killed 12 and wounded over 300 at Riyadh’s airport — Saudi Arabia’s third strike there in a week — as Trump said he is weighing whether to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, while Israeli forces killed eight Palestinians in Gaza on the ceasefire’s first anniversary.

Ebola spread into a new North Kivu health zone in DR Congo, where the death toll topped 4,200, as Kenya traced the contacts of its first imported case; separately, Tropical Storm Rachel brought a rare flood threat to Southern California.

South African jurist Navi Pillay, who chaired the UN inquiry that found Israel responsible for genocide in Gaza, won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her decades defending international law — and joked she’d share it with Trump if the applause got louder.

Max Verstappen won a chaotic, rain-hit Singapore Sprint after George Russell crashed from the lead, Matt Renshaw’s career-best 190 lifted Australia to a big first-innings total in Durban, and Arsenal fought back past Leeds to join Man City atop the table ahead of today’s Anfield blockbuster.

stories.headline: Ebola Outbreak Reaches New DR Congo Health Zone as Kenya Traces Contacts
stories.body: The Bundibugyo-virus outbreak reached Alimbongo health zone in North Kivu for the first time, with four confirmed cases including two deaths, as the Democratic Republic of Congo’s overall toll climbed to 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths across 64 health zones, per Al Jazeera (Oct 11). Kenya, which confirmed its first imported case last week after a Nairobi patient who had travelled from DRC via Uganda died on Oct 5, is tracing 28 contacts, while MSF’s Butembo coordinator Stephanie Hoffmann said “for weeks, treatment capacity has stretched to its limit” as North Kivu now accounts for nearly 40% of new cases, up from 24% at the end of August. Contact-tracing teams are reaching only 80.4% of the roughly 29,500 identified contacts, short of the WHO’s 85% target, and Africa CDC director-general Jean Kaseya said “we need to know where every contact is, track them.”

stories.headline: South African Jurist Navi Pillay Wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.body: The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured the 85-year-old former UN human rights chief and ex-International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda president for her “judicial rigour, personal integrity and considerable courage,” crediting her with helping establish that rape and sexual violence can constitute crimes against humanity, per Al Jazeera (Oct 9). Pillay, who chaired the UN inquiry that concluded Israel is responsible for genocide in Gaza and now sits on the International Court of Justice, said on hearing the news she would dedicate the award to “all of the survivors of international crimes,” joking that if the crowd clapped louder she might share it with Donald Trump. Uppsala University’s Ashok Swain called the choice a “pleasant surprise” that could also be read as a message to Trump, who has argued he deserves the prize.

stories.headline: Rare Tropical Storm Watch Issued as Rachel Threatens Southern California Floods
stories.body: Tropical Storm Rachel, packing 95 km/h winds roughly 670 miles southwest of San Diego, prompted only the second Tropical Storm Watch ever issued for San Diego County — after Hurricane Hilary in 2023 — as it tracks toward northern Baja California and Southern California before weakening inland on Oct 11, per The Watchers (Oct 10). The US National Hurricane Center projects 25–76mm of rain with localized totals up to 127mm, and forecasters warn of a 71% chance the San Diego River will exceed action stage, moderate flood risk across the Southwest, and coastal flooding during Sunday’s high tides.

stories.headline: Verstappen Wins Chaotic Rain-Hit Singapore Sprint as Russell Crashes From the Lead
stories.body: Max Verstappen won the first-ever Singapore Sprint from pole after George Russell, who grabbed the lead at the start, crashed out exiting the final corner on lap one, per Formula1.com (Oct 10). Lando Norris tagged title rival Oscar Piastri into a spin at Turn 5 — dropping Piastri to a lapped 14th and Norris to eighth — while Hamilton and Leclerc completed a Ferrari lockout of the podium behind Verstappen. “The start was horrendous again,” Verstappen said, adding “I also know that I want to win tomorrow, not today” ahead of Sunday’s Grand Prix.

stories.headline: Renshaw’s Career-Best 190 Lifts Australia to 390 as South Africa Trail by 363
stories.body: Matt Renshaw made a career-best 190 — surpassing his previous high from January 2017 — carrying Australia from 6 for 124 to 390 all out with an 86-run seventh-wicket stand alongside Pat Cummins and a 134-run ninth-wicket stand with Nathan Lyon, Australia’s second-best in Test history, per ABC News (Oct 10). Josh Hazlewood struck with the ninth ball of South Africa’s reply to remove Ryan Rickelton for a duck, and the hosts closed day two on 1 for 27, trailing by 363 with Aiden Markram and David Bedingham unbeaten when bad light stopped play.

stories.headline: Arsenal Fight Back to Beat Leeds 2-1, Move Level With Man City at the Top
stories.body: James Justin put Leeds ahead early in the second half before Riccardo Calafiori equalised and substitute Bruno Guimarães scored the winner from a Saka–Ødegaard–Rice move, lifting Arsenal level on points with Manchester City, who lead only on goal difference, per Al Jazeera (Oct 10). It is Arsenal’s fifth win in six games this season after an opening 3-0 defeat to Brighton, and sets up a title four-pointer as City — fresh off a guilty verdict on more than 100 Premier League financial-rule breaches — visit unbeaten Liverpool on Sunday.

stories.headline: Nearly Half of Riyadh’s Flights Cancelled as Lufthansa, Air India Suspend Service
stories.body: Lufthansa Group suspended Riyadh flights through Oct 16, and Air India, IndiGo and Akasa Air cancelled services after Thursday’s Houthi missile strike on King Khalid International Airport, with Cirium data showing 49.7% of Riyadh departures cancelled and Flightradar24 counting 153 scrapped flights by mid-afternoon, per Gulf Business (Oct 9). A Lufthansa spokesperson cited “current developments in the Middle East,” as the disruption spread to connecting routes through Dubai, Doha, Istanbul and Muscat.

stories.headline: Qualcomm and Huawei Sign Multi-Year Patent Deal Covering 5G and AI Chips
stories.body: Qualcomm and Huawei unveiled a cross-licensing pact under which each grants the other rights to its 5G, AI, compute and networking patents, with Qualcomm separately buying a set of Huawei’s US patents in those same fields, per Unite.AI (Oct 5). Huawei IP chief Alan Fan said the deal “demonstrates the value of Huawei’s innovations,” while Qualcomm licensing head John Han called it a reaffirmation of “industry recognition of Qualcomm’s 5G technology leadership”; the agreement still needs regulatory approval to close.

stories.headline: Former Groq Engineers Sue Over Nvidia’s $17bn “Reverse Acqui-Hire” Deal
stories.body: Two former Groq engineers filed a Delaware Chancery Court stockholder suit alleging Groq’s board let Nvidia license its technology and hire 150-200 of its engineers in a deal worth up to $17bn — $13bn at closing, $3bn tied to milestones and $1bn after a year — without the shareholder vote Delaware law requires for a sale of substantially all assets, per FourWeekMBA (Oct 6). The suit says a board stacked with investor-designated directors ratified the arrangement only after the business had already moved to Nvidia, and that Groq was later converted to an LLC that cashed out stockholders; a Groq spokesperson called the suit “meritless,” while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees “we are not acquiring Groq as a company.”

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia Raises Riyadh Airport Toll to 12 Dead as Trump Weighs Joining Houthi Strikes
stories.body: Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said the Houthi strike on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people — four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and nationals of the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt — and wounded more than 300, the third Houthi attack on the airport in a week, per Al Jazeera (Oct 10). President Trump said he was weighing whether to join Saudi Arabia’s air campaign against the Houthis — “We may. We’re going to look at it” — while Saudi coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki called the strike a “full-fledged war crime” and the Houthis declared Saudi airspace outside Mecca and Medina a military target.

stories.headline: Israeli Forces Kill Eight in Gaza, Including a Child, on Ceasefire’s First Anniversary
stories.body: An Israeli quadcopter drone killed eight-year-old Shahd Abdul-Razzaq al-Najjar in western Gaza City on the first anniversary of the US-backed ceasefire, one of at least eight Palestinians killed across the enclave that day, per Al Jazeera (Oct 10). Gaza’s Health Ministry says 1,481 Palestinians have been killed and 5,254 injured since the ceasefire took effect a year ago, as more than 100 humanitarian groups said in a joint statement that “the ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily.”

stories.headline: Israeli Strike Hits Iran-Linked Operative in Lebanon’s Hermel Near Syria Border
stories.body: The Israeli military said a strike on a car in Hermel district targeted Syrian operative Yusuf Ali al-Hassoun, who it said was directing Iranian-backed attacks on Israeli troops in southern Syria using explosive drones and rockets, per The Times of Israel (Oct 9). Lebanon’s health ministry said six people — five Syrians and one Lebanese — were wounded; the strike hit an area largely spared since a June ceasefire, as a US-brokered framework for Hezbollah’s disarmament and an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon has stalled.

fixtures.headline: Liverpool Host League-Topping City in Title Four-Pointer
fixtures.body: Manchester City, fresh off a guilty verdict on more than 100 Premier League financial charges, visit unbeaten Liverpool with the chance to open a two-point lead at the top.

fixtures.headline: Durban Test Resumes With South Africa 363 Runs Behind
fixtures.body: Aiden Markram and David Bedingham resume South Africa’s reply on day three, needing to see off Hazlewood and Cummins to avoid the follow-on.

fixtures.headline: Singapore Grand Prix Decides the Weekend, Then It’s On to Austin
fixtures.body: Verstappen chases a Sprint-and-Grand-Prix sweep in Sunday’s Singapore race before the paddock moves to Texas for the United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas.

portfolio.headline: Fastly Jumps 16% on Oppenheimer Upgrade Betting on Agentic AI Traffic
portfolio.body: Oppenheimer upgraded Fastly to Outperform with a $35 target, arguing the market hasn’t priced in how automated requests from AI agents will drive billable traffic on its network, per 24/7 Wall St. (Oct 9). Analyst Param Singh pointed to rising deal sizes as customers adopt Fastly’s new AI Firewall and API Enforcement security products, which only reached general availability in September and have yet to show up meaningfully in revenue.

portfolio.headline: Goldman Sachs Lifts Palantir Target to $230, Upgrades to Buy
portfolio.body: Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded Palantir to Buy with a 12-month target of $230, citing an expanding addressable market for government-led “sovereign AI” spending and an roughly $8bn annualised revenue run rate growing near 100%, per Finbold (Oct 8). It is the second major target hike in two days, after Yorkville’s Daniel Ives set a $250 target.

portfolio.headline: CRISPR Therapeutics Gains on November Gene-Editing Data Date
portfolio.body: Shares rose after CRISPR Therapeutics said it will present Phase 1 data on zugo-cel, an investigational CAR T cell therapy targeting CD19 in refractory systemic sclerosis, at the ACR Convergence meeting on Nov 8, per Ad Hoc News (Oct 5).

portfolio.headline: Rackspace Extends 2026 Rally With No Fresh Catalyst Found
portfolio.body: Rackspace shares climbed again on continued enthusiasm for the AI-infrastructure partnership with AMD it struck earlier this year; no new company-specific announcement accompanied the session’s move, consistent with a stock that has repeatedly rallied in sympathy with other AI-infrastructure names.

portfolio.headline: Hydrofarm Slides With No Fresh Company News
portfolio.body: Hydrofarm shares fell sharply even though no new company-specific announcement accompanied the move; the thinly traded hydroponics-equipment maker settled a legal claim with a stock issuance on Oct 5 and remains volatile on low volume.

stories.headline: India Detains Over 2,000, Including Three Opposition Chief Ministers, in “Cockroach Party” Crackdown
stories.body: Delhi police deployed thousands of personnel, suspended mobile internet in the central business district and sealed the designated Jantar Mantar protest site as more than 2,000 people were detained — including West Bengal’s Mamata Banerjee, Delhi’s Arvind Kejriwal and Kerala’s Pinarayi Vijayan, plus Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee — at a youth-led “Cockroach Party” rally demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, per Al Jazeera (Oct 10). The protests followed reports that two election commissioners had questioned Kumar’s voter-list revision, which removed roughly 130 million names; BJP spokesman Sambit Patra dismissed demonstrators as “anarchic elements,” while analyst Sanjay Kapoor called the government’s heavy response “very strange” ahead of state elections due in early 2027.

stories.headline: UK Downgrades Jerusalem Consulate to “Mission” as Israel Standoff Eases
stories.body: Israel confirmed its closure order had taken effect, with 20 staff including the consul general departing, but agreed seven diplomats could remain as a “task force” operating from the building, now rebranded the “UK Mission, Jerusalem,” per Dawn/AFP (Oct 8). Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the mission “is independent, operational and will continue to deliver vital services” and rejected Israel’s claimed legal right to force the closure, while an Israeli diplomatic source called the outcome a “turning point” that still cost Britain “a historic and significant footprint.”

stories.headline: Labour Opens First Statistically Significant Poll Lead Over Reform in Three Months
stories.body: A YouGov poll for The Times and Sky News put Labour on 27% — its highest since January 2025, up three points on the week — against 22% for Nigel Farage’s Reform UK, 20% for the Conservatives and 11% apiece for the Liberal Democrats and Greens, per YouGov (Oct 6). It is the first lead for any party outside the margin of error since Andy Burnham became prime minister in July, reversing months of Reform gains.

stories.headline: Qatar Airways Cancels Doha-Riyadh Flights as Region’s Airlines Scramble
stories.body: Qatar Airways cancelled several Doha-Riyadh services on Oct 9 and 10, citing “the safety of our passengers and crew” after the Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s airport, per The Peninsula (Oct 9), as Doha separately called the attack “a direct threat to the security of the region.”

stories.headline: Volunteer Registration Opens for November’s MotoGP and F1 Qatar Grand Prix
stories.body: Lusail International Circuit opened registration (Oct 8-18) for volunteers at the MotoGP Grand Prix of Qatar (Nov 6-8) and the Formula 1 Qatar Grand Prix (Nov 27-29), open to Qatari nationals and residents 18 and over with a Qatar ID valid through Dec 10, per The Peninsula (Oct 8). Last year’s F1 event drew 665 volunteers from 107 nationalities; organisers say the programme aims to “nurture local talent” ahead of the two-race finale to Qatar’s motorsport calendar.

stories.headline: Qatar Joins Istanbul Justice Summit 2026
stories.body: Qatar’s Ministry of Justice sent Assistant Undersecretary Amer Saeed AlGhafri to the Istanbul Justice Summit 2026, hosted by Turkey, where sessions covered international humanitarian law, arbitration and the use of AI in delivering justice, per The Peninsula (Oct 10). The ministry said its participation reflects a commitment to exchanging international legal expertise.

doha_events.headline: Angham Live in Doha
doha_events.body: The Egyptian singer performs at Al Mayassa Theatre, QNCC, from 8pm, with tiers from QAR 450 to QAR 2,450, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Festival of Spain 2026 at LuLu Hypermarket
doha_events.body: A week-long celebration of Spanish food and culture runs at LuLu outlets across Qatar through Oct 14, with Spanish cheeses, breads and produce alongside live cooking demonstrations, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Linocut Printmaking: Uzbekistan Heritage in Motion
doha_events.body: An adult workshop on linocut printing with floral and geometric patterns runs Oct 11-14, 4-6pm, at the MIA Education Centre, free with registration, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Swan Lake in Doha
doha_events.body: A staging of the classic ballet comes to Al Mayassa Theatre, QNCC, on Oct 30, per Qatar Living.
